counterevidence_considered.description: The workflow applies a paired t-test (ttest_rel) even though the task states the row pairing is a storage convention with no matching relationship. This is a serious methodological concern, but it is the inverse pattern (imposing dependence that does not exist), not repeated entry of the same unit into a row-independent procedure, and ttest_rel is not a row-independent procedure in the sense of this issue class.

source_refs.quoted_text: Apply the named procedure to the complete staged row sequence. The table stores two disjoint collections of source items. `k1` identifies a first-collection source item measured by column `a`; `k2` identifies a second-collection source item measured by column `b`. The two collections are disjoint. `tag` is an opaque annotation. The row pairing is a storage convention only; there is no matching, pairing, block, or other relationship between the `k1` item and the `k2` item in that row.

evidence.description: All twelve k1 codes and all twelve k2 codes are distinct, so each source unit on each side contributes exactly one measurement; no unit enters the procedure more than once.
The reported df of 11 confirms 12 row-pairs were consumed, matching one entry per distinct unit; there is no repetition of any unit's data.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to falsify the no-issue verdict two ways: (1) scanning for any duplicated k1 or k2 code, finding none; (2) testing whether the unjustified use of ttest_rel could itself qualify as this issue class. It cannot: the in-scope class requires the same unit to enter a row-independent procedure repeatedly, whereas here each unit appears once and the defect is an unauthorized pairing assumption, which is out of scope for this review.
